metadata.description: Files and patterns to exclude when updating branches from template

notes.how_it_works: Two types of exclusions during branch updates:

ignore_files.purpose: Template-internal management files that branches don't need

ignore_patterns.description: Glob patterns - matches filenames AND directory names
ignore_patterns.purpose: Exclude generated files, caches, and user content markers
how_matching_works: Step 1: Check if filename matches pattern (e.g., file.pyc matches *.pyc)
Step 2: Check if any parent directory matches (e.g., files inside __pycache__/ dir)

notes.what_gets_ignored: These files never copy to branches during updates - they stay template-only

starter_tests.why_the_test_files_are_here: These two files SHIP AT CREATE - a newborn gets them and needs them, they are what carries test_quality from 15% to 100% at birth. They are listed here because seedgo's architecture baseline treats every file in this template as a structural requirement of EVERY branch of this class, and starter tests are not that: a mature branch replaces them with its own suite, exactly as spawn's README already documents for test_scaffold.py.
starter_tests.what_happens_without_this_entry: Measured 2026-08-22: adding these two files to the template and running the CI gate (.github/scripts/seedgo_audit.py) dropped 9 existing branches from 100% to 99% with 'Missing file: tests/test_cli_routing.py' - aipass, canary, cli, commons, flow, hooks, memory, seedgo, trigger. The gate floor is 100 and it exits 1, so a template addition reds the whole board without touching a single branch's code.
starter_tests.scope_of_this_list: ignore_files is honoured by seedgo's architecture baseline (matched on basename). spawn's create copies these files regardless - .registry_ignore.json and .template_registry.json are themselves in this list and both land in every newborn, which is the proof. The 'never copy during updates' note below describes update behaviour, not create.
